scope: Twenty-sixth expansion batch: 12 controlled relation/attachment exercises. Three shared kurai/gurai/hodo degree illustrations contrast with three clausal noni counterexpectations; three noun-based kurai/gurai low-bar minimums contrast with three nominal noni counterexpectations. This is three dedicated degree and three dedicated minimum items, not six independent kurai/hodo word distinctions or a complete noni curriculum.

sources.publisher: Shogakukan, Digital Daijisen and Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten via Kotobank
sources.section: Actual HTML: Daijisen heading くらい【位】［副助］, not the preceding rank noun, kanji entry or i counter. Sense2 uses a situation as a degree standard, including koemo-denai-kurai bikkuri-shita; sense3 covers evaluative emphasis and a kurai-nara example. Separately, Seisenban Kokugo's [2] particle sense2 and its 語誌 note3 explicitly exclude the downplaying use from replacement by hodo. Do not misdescribe Daijisen's kurai-nara example as a direct attestation of every minimum request, or import Kokugo's Edo-period voicing tendencies as modern rules.

Actual lesson HTML: formation, meaning, examples and comparison table. Tears-of-joy and desire-based degree examples support illustrative situations, and the degree row accepts both kurai and hodo. The linked downplaying lesson distinguishes a modest/easy item. Do NOT adopt the page's categorical ban on kurai for high degree or every negative superlative: Daijisen itself has strong surprise and a dog-loyalty superlative example. Broad frequency/formality claims were not needed.

Actual lesson HTML, ～ぐらい/～くらい（軽視）: the speaker considers something easy, minor or unimportant. Inspected email, simple food preparation, hiragana and household-task examples; direct noun attachment. This supports the speaker-evaluated low bar, not a neutral numerical lower-bound operator or a guarantee that the task is objectively easy for every person. Historical or blanket voicing rules and the comparison table's unrelated universal prohibitions are not adopted.

Exact particle entry with readings kurai/gurai, not the rank noun: sense2 to-the-extent/so-that/at-least, and note also written as 位. Sense1 approximate quantity and sense3 comparison are distinct uses. A gloss 'at least' alone does not establish a hard numerical minimum.
Exact 程/hodo entry, particle sense7 for degree/as much as, usually kana. Not the adjacent 歩度 homophone or the noun senses. Sense8 correlated change does not create a substitution rule with kurai.

Using のに to mean despite, including the actual HTML examples following a past plain verb and a noun + na. The earlier attachment reminder for nouns/na-adjectives supplies the same na rule. Simplified extraction omitted Japanese, so the examples were read in the actual HTML. Only concessive attachment and relation are adopted. The page's unrelated te-form tense descriptions are outside scope; its initial contradiction shorthand for ga/kedo is explicitly qualified later and is not treated here as a universal rule.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original and need independent linguistic review, including all39 accepted literal completions, complete prompts and answer-only explanations. Three degree situations are sleep difficulty, speechless surprise and desire to rewatch; three minimums are a practiced name, a rehearsed greeting and familiar tea preparation.

The first six visibly name bare kurai/gurai/hodo versus kana connective noni, without added wa. The last six name kurai/gurai with optional wa versus the standard plain nonpast noun-predicate ending nanoni. These are controlled relationship and attachment choices; other connectors, fuller minimum framings such as dake-wa, topic-marked degree expressions and different tense forms are outside the stated tasks, not ungrammatical Japanese.

Kurai/gurai/hodo degree equivalents share one target and five literal spellings. One model shows each kana particle; this does not independently discriminate the particles. Minimum answers accept kurai/gurai and the 位 spelling with or without wa, six strings per item. Noni has three clause and three noun-predicate targets, requiring noni and nanoni respectively.

The low-bar items evaluate the speaker's own practiced ability or modest contribution. They do not imply that writing a name, greeting people or preparing tea is universally easy. Explain potential reproach when the same 'something as basic as' stance is aimed at another person; it is not always rude, and a polite ending alone does not guarantee a tactful request.

Do not teach all kurai degree as slight, all degree standards as actual events, every noni result as bad, or a main-clause past tense as forcing every subordinate predicate into past tense. The written-help counterexpectation has an appreciated result. The degree video describes desire without asserting completed repeat viewings.

The noun pairs retain name/greeting/tea while changing the discourse relationship. Familiar tea provides a speaker expectation, not a universal guarantee about taste. The sleeplessness example is an individual surprising report, not a health claim or advice to avoid sleep.

Keep noun-based low-bar assessment distinct from an estimated quantity such as san-pun-kurai and from an exact numerical lower bound such as san-pun-ijou. This batch does not claim all evaluative kurai uses, the kurai-nara preference pattern, or purpose/resource noni are independently practiced.

Retrieval pitfalls: bare Kotobank /word/くらい redirected to a mixed cry/historical cross-reference page. Followed its actual 位 link to429901 and inspected the particle sections. Search summaries supplied mismatched site URLs, unsupported book attributions and a false strict-only analysis of dake-wa; those were not used. The applied-linguistics page could not be retrieved by either web fetch or Python TLS, so its content was not adopted. Bunpro /のに led to its purpose lesson and /だけは to possible extent; neither supplies the primary evidence needed here.

The shared authoring contract gains one grounded note from the preceding possible-extent batch: test the defining relationship rather than a surface proxy, and consider matched outcomes with distinct contextual explanations. Existing answer-class, literal-blank, source-verification and rare-spelling guidance already covers those issues and is not duplicated in another guide.

All329 prior exercise records and IDs remain unchanged. Add one scoped article subsection and reference bullet, matching README/contract scope and focused regressions; retain one SRS identity per exercise. No Android, counter, schema or grading changes. Broader mixed selection remains the next planned gap after this bounded degree/minimum coverage.
